I can't confirm or rule out option a, or any other option. I don't give quiz answers before grading, and that includes a "just checking" on one option. Quiz 0001 hasn't been graded, so the item is still closed. A TA's okay doesn't change how I handle it here. If you want certainty before you hand it in, ask your TA directly.

Here are two things you can do yourself:

- **Walk the scenario step by step.** The student asks about the laser cutter, and the model decides it needs `check_calendar`. Write down who does what, in order: what the model produces, what the program around it does, and what the calendar system does. Then check each option against your own list.
- **Test each option.** Ask whether it describes something a language model can do, since the model only takes text in and writes text out. This test applies to every option the same way, so it doesn't favor any of them.

Try writing your reasoning for why you picked a, in a sentence or two, and for why you'd reject the others. Writing it out will show you how sure you are. It will also help with the short-answer items, q5 and q6, which ask for exactly this kind of explanation.

Once the quiz is graded, I'll go through q2 with you in full, including why each wrong option is tempting.

Which part of the loop are you least sure about: what the model writes, or what the program does with it?
